sources.headline: India’s Cockroach movement says members detained as protests continue
sources.text: India’s opposition and student-led CJP movement demand election chief’s resignation, plan mass demonstration on Saturday.India’s Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) says that authorities have detained many of its members as thousands of the group’s supporters and members of several student groups continue to protest, demanding the election chief’s resignation.Thursday’s demonstrations come ahead of CJP-led antigovernment protests planned for Saturday, with thousands expected to march to Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site in the capital, New Delhi.Ashutosh Ranka, a spokesperson for the movement, said in a post on X on Thursday that “at least 10,000” people from CJP demonstrations, student organisations, affiliated grassroots groups and political parties had been detained across the country.Among those arrested is CJP national spokesman Deepak Baliyan, who was taken into police custody on Thursday, according to the group’s statements.Al Jazeera could not immediately verify the claims, but videos posted on X showed activists being taken away in vans.Opposition parties and students affiliated with the CJP movement have been demanding the resignation of the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, over a controversial revision of voter lists.They accuse the poll body he heads of benefitting Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).A man walks past a graffiti-marked poster of India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a protest by the opposition alliance in New Delhi on October 8, 2026, calling for the resignation of the country’s chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar [Arun Sankar/AFP]On Thursday, CJP said that among those detained was ‌a group of students from the city of Pune who were headed for New Delhi to participate in planned protests at the iconic Jantar Mantar observatory. CJP said they were taken away in a bus to an unknown location.“Why not just declare EMERGENCY?” CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said in a response to a post with a video of activists being detained.‘Every vote matters’India’s Election Commission has so far removed more than 130 million names from the voter lists, with millions appealing the removals. About 969 million people were eligible to vote in the 2024 election.Protesters allege the changes disproportionately removed voters who support opposition parties while preserving or adding voters more likely to back Modi’s party.The commission and government deny the allegations. They say the revision has no political motive but is aimed at removing duplicate and ineligible entries while ensuring eligible voters remain registered.Earlier on Thursday, thousands of supporters of the CJP youth movement protested in the tech hub of Bengaluru.Many of the protesters held posters that said, “Every name counts, Every vote matters” and “Stop the Murder of ⁠Democracy”.Khushi Shrivastava, a 22-year-old architecture student at the protest, told the Reuters news agency: “I think voting right is the most basic point of democracy … People ⁠who actually want to vote, who actually care about the future of India, they are just being [denied] voting rights.”India’s Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi waves from a bus during a protest by the opposition alliance in New Delhi on October 8, 2026 [Arun Sankar/AFP]On Wednesday, Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi was briefly detained for the third time in two days, as his Congress ‌Party accused police of using “brute force”.Police said the allegations were being used to “defame” them. BJP’s spokesperson ‌Gaurav ‌Bhatia said the allegations were “being levelled by an irresponsible, anarchist opposition”.

sources.headline: Indian Opposition Leaders Detained as Protests Over Voter Rolls Intensify
sources.text: Lawmakers in the capital were forcibly removed for a second consecutive day as police cracked down on demonstrations against the deletion of voter names.

sources.headline: Indian opposition MPs detained in protest against election chief
sources.text: Delhi witnessed dramatic scenes on Tuesday night when police broke up a protest by opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and other MPs who were seeking the resignation of India's top election official over a controversial voter roll revision.Videos showing police forcing Gandhi on to a bus and preventing him from climbing out of the bus window subsequently went viral on social media.The protest marks a fresh escalation in the opposition's standoff with the Election Commission.Opposition parties accuse Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar of revising electoral rolls to benefit India's governing Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Both the BJP and the commission have rejected the allegation.Gandhi, his sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other MPs sat in protest at a nearby building for the entire day after they were stopped during their march to the Election Commission's office.The commission said it was willing to meet the opposition, but objected to their proposed 240-member delegation meeting at the parliament.In a statement released on Tuesday night, it said that a party representative must request an appointment and that meetings are held at the commission. Gandhi had said earlier in the day that the opposition simply wanted to meet the election commissioners and ask questions about the voter roll revision."We are all opposition MPs... and we just want to speak with them," he told reporters. "I do not know why the Election Commission does not want to talk to us."News agency ANI, citing a statement from the police, reported that the protesters were removed "to maintain law and order and prevent the situation from escalating".A police complaint has also been registered against the Gandhis for entering Akashvani Bhavan (or the Broadcasting House) without permission, PTI news agency reported. Security was tightened around the Election Commission headquarters on Tuesday, with police barricading roads along the route between parliament and the commission's office. Police officers, some carrying batons and wearing body cameras, reportedly outnumbered protesters along the route to the poll panel's office. In the afternoon, they detained several MPs who tried to take alternative routes to reach the commission, police official Manjeet Sheoran told the BBC."They were picked up in buses and taken to different police stations," he said.The Gandhi siblings were also detained and taken away in a police bus, but were released shortly afterwards. They then resumed their march before staging a sit-in at Akashvani Bhavan near the Election Commission headquarters.Police did not say how many lawmakers were detained. The opposition said 237 MPs from several parties took part in the march.Tuesday's protest came just four days after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a Gen Z-backed online satirical movement, organised demonstrations in Mumbai and Delhi, also demanding the CEC's resignation. The group has described those demonstrations as the beginning of a nationwide campaign and has called for another round of protests on 10 October.At the centre of the controversy is the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The exercise began in the eastern state of Bihar in June 2025 before being expanded to other parts of the country. The commission says the revision is intended to remove duplicate and ineligible voters from electoral rolls. More than 130 million names have so far been removed from draft voter lists nationwide.Opposition parties and activists allege that many eligible voters have been excluded and accuse the poll panel of conducting the process improperly.The campaign against Kumar gathered momentum after an investigation by the Indian Express newspaper reported that election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over a 10-month period to decisions and orders they said had been issued in the commission's name without their knowledge.According to the report, the objections related to issues including additions and deletions from voter rolls, access to the voter database and the security of electoral data. The three-member commission, comprising the CEC and two election commissioners, defended its decision-making process, saying differing views were part of institutional functioning and that decisions had ultimately been taken unanimously.The revelations nevertheless triggered a political backlash, with opposition leaders intensifying calls for Kumar's resignation.

Published: 8:01pm, 6 Oct 2026

Indian police detained several opposition lawmakers in the capital of New Delhi on Tuesday for trying to breach barricades during a protest march to demand the resignation of the election chief over a controversial revision of voter lists.

The march presents a fresh political challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi midway into his ‌third term, just months after similar protests forced the resignation of his education minister over exam paper leaks.

Parties opposing Modi’s government along with members of the popular “cockroach” youth movement protested against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar after the Indian Express newspaper reported divisions in the poll body last month.

The reported differences over the lists and voter registration procedures stoked concern about the neutrality of the commission, led by a Modi government appointee.

Members of the National Students’ Union of India hold placards during a protest at Freedom Park in Bengaluru, India, on Tuesday. Photo: EPA

“The election commission is a puppet in the hands of the government,” Congress ⁠president Mallikarjun Kharge, told reporters as the march began. “We are fighting to save our democracy.”

Lawmakers carried placards, waved ‌the national flag and shouted slogans against Kumar during the march, roughly 1km long, or less than a mile, to the Election Commission headquarters from parliament, through the centre of Delhi.

Some carried placards calling Kumar a ‌traitor and accused the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of snatching away the right to vote, while they sat on the road outside ⁠the panel’s office, demanding to ⁠meet him.

Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, his sister Priyanka and several more stood on police barricades there, waving the national flag and calling for Kumar to resign.

Hundreds of ‌security personnel, some wearing riot gear and carrying batons, tried to stop Gandhi and other lawmakers from entering the election commission.

Police did not immediately comment on the detentions.

“After failing multiple times, Congress leaders have decided to establish anarchy in the country and attack institutions,” BJP spokesman Sambit Patra told ‌reporters before Tuesday’s protest.

Supporters gather with Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, as they take part in a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in New Delhi on Tuesday. Photo: Reuters

TV channels said the Gandhi siblings were among those briefly detained before being released.

The duo sought entry through the grounds ⁠of the state radio office next door, where they sat in protest under a tree after the route was blocked, the channels ⁠said.

Congress and other parties say the revised voter lists benefit Modi and his party. Kumar has not commented on the issue, but the commission and Modi’s BJP denied the accusations.

Tuesday’s event is the latest of a series of ‌almost daily demonstrations by student organisations, political ‌parties and the “cockroach” movement, which began last week.

India’s Supreme Court agreed on Monday to hear requests for its intervention in the accusations against the poll body’s voter drive, and the conduct of its chief.

If “there are decisions against the law … We will take care of it,” the court said at the hearing, after the petitioners accused the poll body of bias.
